summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The national frame is what matters here: the 2025 hate-crime record (227 murders, +62% on 2024, most perpetrators police or public-space strangers) and the February 2025 presidential decrees cutting the Gender Identity Law apply in Tucumán as elsewhere, while the province carries neither the metros' trans sex-work policing nor a documented community presence - and the dossier cautions that at these numbers a single provincial case is a real signal, so a zero should not be read as safety.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (uncached; no dossier annotation line); from its masthead the article (10 April 2025) reports Argentina's transgender community describing a chaotic, desperate situation under the national policy reversal.

Presentes report (March 2026) on the National Observatory of Hate Crimes' annual record: 227 reported hate crimes against LGBT+ people in 2025, +62% on 2024 and the highest in the Observatory's ten years - one every 38 hours, most perpetrators security force members or unidentified street attackers, institutional violence quadrupling (17 cases in 2024 to 64 in 2025), with police interventions in three provinces among the November 2025 deaths and fresh assaults in early 2026 including the killing of a Jujuy-based collective president.

NOTE: English page not retrievable at fetch time (uncached; the fetched Spanish original is cited in the dossier): the February 2025 decree (DNU 62/2025) amending the Gender Identity Law to bar hormonal and surgical transition treatment for under-18s - plus a parallel decree requiring birth-sex prison placement - with a judge suspending the decree within a week, the government appealing, and the ruling front-loaded on the eve of the presidential trip.
